2015_077_030315mtg.paragraph: Regular meeting agenda packet of the Troy School District Board of Education for March 3, 2015, convening at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The packet pairs recognition items and the January 2015 Treasurer's Report with the fiscal year's first General Fund budget amendment, which raises budgeted revenues and incoming transfers from $131,253,100 to $142,706,181, appropriates $143,627,633, and projects an ending fund balance of $20,458,563 at June 30. Also before the Board are bond-funded equipment awards of $786,365 for Athens High School and $420,800 for chillers, a special education programming report, open-enrollment closures for 2015/2016, and first readings of four board policies.

**Meeting** — Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, March 3, 2015, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition** — Senior Scholar Athletes 2014-15, for winter and spring sport seniors holding a 3.5 cumulative grade point average; Fall 2014 All-State athletes including Alexander Balte, Nathaniel Bladecki, Jennifer Cui and Vincent Thieu; a Mission Moment for Martell Elementary's Leader in Me program, funded by grants securing over $50,000; a resolution naming February Principal Appreciation Month; and third-year Spirit of Diversity Awards.

**Consent agenda** — February 10, 2015 meeting and workshop minutes plus the January 2015 Treasurer's Report. That meeting ran 5:30 p.m. to 5:45 p.m. under President Philippart with Trustee Miletti absent; Resolutions 15-017 through 15-021 each carried Yes 6, No 0, covering consent items, personnel, a bargaining team led by Barb Ruga of Clark Hill, PC for TEA, TESA and TESPA contracts expiring June 30, 2015, and Section 22f best practices certification ($50 per pupil, at least 7 of 9 criteria by June 1, 2015, MCL 388.1622f).

State revenue rose 7.6% on actual State Aid Status Report figures: 22a Prop A obligation $2,491,157 reflecting a $50 increase in the per pupil foundation allowance, 22b discretionary payment $631,434, 147C MPSERS UAAL rate stabilization (4.56% to 7.63%) $3,306,660, and the 22f best practice incentive ($52 to $50) ($27,907). Closing the Durant Fund adds $5,619,125 on both sides. Amended revenue by source is Local 9%, State 63%, Federal 2%, incoming transfers and other 26%; expense by object is salaries 48%, benefits 29%, purchased services 12%.

**Special education** — Shawna Veit reported 1,250 students with IEPs and 550 service-only students, with teacher FTE of 52.8 plus 16.3 teacher consultants, 14.1 speech and language pathologists, 11.4 social workers and 7.3 psychologists; center program usage was 106 in 2004-2005, 90 in 2009-2010 and 61 in 2014-2015. Oakland County has 28 school districts, 22,556 students with IEPs and 1,030 served in center programs.

**Bond and business actions** — Athens High School mechanical and electrical pre-purchase totaling $786,365.00 (ThermalNetics $382,000.00 and $164,000.00; Madison/Schneider Electric $240,265.00), and chiller equipment for Athens High, Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools to ThermalNetics for Daikin/McQuay at $420,800.00 — both from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Bemis, Schroeder, Athens High and Troy High close to open enrollment for 2015/2016, except up to 25 incoming ninth graders applying to Athens between March 4 and March 31, 2015.

**Policy first readings** — B-0102 (six-year terms beginning November 2016, even years), B-1202 (place of meeting, twenty-four hours' notice), B-1204 (four members constitute a quorum; remote participation without voting; Open Meetings Act, MCL 15.261 et seq.), and B-1211, which replaces two 30-minute public participation periods with a single 60-minute limit per meeting and keeps three-minute speaker turns.

**Identity and logistics.** Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, March 3, 2015 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district administration at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools. Packet page footers run through 151.

**Recognition.** Senior Scholar Athletes 2014-15 honors winter and spring sport seniors who maintained a 3.5 cumulative grade point average at Troy High School, Athens High School and the International Academy, with names read by Mr. Jolly. Fall 2014 All-State athletes: Alexander Balte, Michael Faber, Jason Potter and Vincent Thieu (boys tennis), Nathaniel Bladecki and Torin Gebauer (boys soccer), Jennifer Cui (girls golf) and Kunai Tangri (cross country). The TSD Mission Moment honors Martell Elementary for implementing Leader in Me, based on Stephen Covey's "7 Habits of Highly Effective People"; a summer 2014 book study led to grants securing over $50,000 and over five days of training, with advisors Chuck Lesser, Sue Delbeke and Stacey Schoenherr. February is recognized as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy. The third-year Spirit of Diversity Awards, designed by the Troy Diversity & Inclusion Council and read by Kerry Birmingham, go to Nancy Lining, Dawn Hayes, Jen Hilzinger, Kerry Brennan, Lori Medina-Yashinsky, Lisa Carruthers, Stephanie Sacco and Nadeen Brown for work including Larson Strong, the Religious Diversity Journeys Program, Fred Korematsu Day, Cultural Connection and "Leopard Links."

**February 10, 2015 minutes.** President Philippart called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m. at the Administration Building with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Schmidt and Underwood present and Trustee Miletti absent; Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Haezebrouck and West attended, with TMP Architects, Barton Malow and approximately 12 members of the audience. Resolution 15-017 (Hauff/Edmunds) approved consent items: January 13, 2015 regular and closed session minutes, January 20, 2015 workshop minutes, January 24, 2015 retreat minutes and the December 2014 Treasurer's Report. Resolution 15-018 (Schmidt/Fleming) approved personnel including new hire Kellene Hilliard. Resolution 15-019 (Edmunds/Hauff) named Barb Ruga of Clark Hill, PC chief spokesperson with Mark Dziatczak, Mary Haezebrouck, Larry Lobert and Rick West for negotiations with TEA/MEA/NEA, TESA/MEA/NEA and TESPA/MEA/NEA, all contracts expiring June 30, 2015. Resolution 15-020 (Fleming/Underwood) accepted an administrative resignation. Resolution 15-021 (Underwood/Fleming) certified compliance under Section 22f of the State School Aid Act, providing $50 per pupil one-time grants to districts meeting at least 7 of 9 best practices criteria by June 1, 2015 (MCL 388.1622f), citing Section 105 or 105c enrollment (MCL 388.1705) and section 15(3) of 1947 PA 336 (MCL 423.215). All votes were Yes 6, No 0, Miletti absent; adjournment at 5:45 p.m., Paula Fleming, Secretary. The workshop that evening ran 5:49 p.m. to 8:29 p.m.

**Item 7.A – open enrollment, 2015/2016.** Administration recommends closing Bemis and Schroeder Elementary Schools on enrollment and physical space grounds and closing Athens High School and Troy High School, except for not more than 25 incoming ninth grade students residing in the Troy High attendance area who wish to attend Athens; applications are accepted March 4 through March 31, 2015. Students with siblings attending Athens High and enrolled in grades 9-11 may open enroll to Athens.

**Item 7.B – Oakland County Special Education Programming.** Presented by Mrs. Shawna Veit, Supervisor of Special Education, in a deck titled "Special Education in Troy: Past, Present, Future…" framed as an outcome of the Oakland County Center Program Redesign. Troy serves 1,250 students with IEPs. Early On (birth–3) has 1.4 teacher FTE and 30 children; the Early Childhood Program (2½–5) 2.0 FTE and 38. Elementary: Resource Room (cross categorical) 30.2 FTE and 461 children; autism spectrum disorder 5.0 FTE and 22; mild cognitive impairment 7.6 FTE and 76; moderate cognitive impairment 3.0 FTE and 29. Post-high: Troy Center for Transition 3.0 FTE and 40 students; Project Search – Troy Beaumont 1.0 FTE and 10. Service-only students, not assigned to a special education program, number 550. Professional staff FTE: teacher 52.8, teacher consultant 16.3, speech and language pathologist 14.1, school social worker 11.4, school psychologist 7.3, transition coordinator 1.0, curriculum and instruction coordination 1.0, assistive technology 1.4, occupational and physical therapists 6.4. Support staff FTE: para educator 31.5, student aide 88.0, job coach 3.9, post high program assistant 5.0. Countywide there are 28 school districts, 22,556 students with IEPs (about 10% of total students) and 1,030 served in center programs. Troy center program usage was 106 in 2004-2005, 90 in 2009-2010 and 61 in 2014-2015. Projected post-high population: 45 in 2015-2016, 60 in 2016-2017, 72 in 2017-2018, 86 in 2018-2019, 88 in 2019-2020, 97 in 2020-2021, 104 in 2021-2022. OCSA endorsed recommendations in October 2013 with the complex-needs census completed 2014. The report states 99% of students with disabilities receive some on-grade-level math instruction at the elementary level, and sets a departmental program review through February with recommendations in Spring 2015.

**Items 8.A and 8.B – 2014-15 General Fund Budget Amendment.** State revenue increased 7.6% on actual State Aid Status Report figures: 22a Prop A obligation $2,491,157 tied to a $50 increase in the per pupil foundation allowance; 22b discretionary payment $631,434; 147C MPSERS UAAL rate stabilization categorical moving 4.56% to 7.63% for $3,306,660; and the 22f best practice incentive falling from $52 to $50 for ($27,907). Incoming transfers rise for closing of the Durant Fund at $5,619,125; out of district tuition falls ($394,235) and Special Ed Public Act 18 revenue ($192,962). Benefits reflect the MPSERS UAAL rate plus a 2.3% increase in the hard cap rate; capital outlay increases to match TRIG grant revenue; other expenses decrease ($1.2 million) for anticipated tax abatement write-offs. Amended revenue by source: Local 9%, State 63%, Federal 2%, incoming transfers and other 26%. Expense by object: salaries 48%, benefits 29%, purchased services 12%, outgoing transfers and other 6%, supplies 5%, capital outlay 0%, other 0%. The General Fund is amended three times a year (December, March, June), special revenue funds twice (February, June). Revenues are amended from $36,487,546 to $36,436,455 local (($51,091)), $83,797,430 to $90,201,335 state (6,403,905), $3,346,213 to $3,414,552 federal (68,339) and $7,621,911 to $12,653,839 incoming transfers/other (5,031,928), for total revenues of $142,706,181 versus $131,253,100 approved, a change of $11,453,081; with fund balance July 1 restated from $19,312,628 to $21,380,015, total available to appropriate is $164,086,196 versus $150,565,728. Of that, $143,627,633 is appropriated: instruction basic programs $75,638,746 (change $4,397,205), added needs $16,587,067, adult/continuing education $727,069, total instruction $92,952,882; support services pupil $10,439,856, instructional staff $6,990,809, general administration $1,779,669, school administration $7,880,000, business services $1,428,229, operations/maintenance $9,200,215, pupil transportation $3,483,130, central services $1,846,931, athletics and other $1,823,265, total support services $44,872,104; community services $146,010; outgoing transfers/other $5,656,637. Excess revenues/(expenditures) moves from ($1,272,080) to ($921,452) and ending fund balance June 30 from $18,040,548 to $20,458,563, a change of $2,418,015.

**Items 8.C and 8.D – bond equipment awards.** Bids for pre-purchase of mechanical and electrical equipment for the Athens MEP upgrade, reviewed by Mr. Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations, are awarded from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund: central HVAC equipment to ThermalNetics at $382,000.00, air/air energy recovery equipment to Thermalnetics at $164,000.00, and secondary unit substitutions to Madison/Schneider Electric at $240,265.00, totaling $786,365.00. Chiller equipment for Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools and Athens High School goes to ThermalNetics, distributor for Daikin/McQuay, at $420,800.00. Mr. Carson's February 25, 2015 memorandum to Superintendent Rich Machesky, from Operations at 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083 (Ph 248.823.4050, Fax 248.823.4077), states Bid Category 236426 covers air cooled rotary screw water chillers and the RFP resulted in 4 bids with Daikin/McQuay the low qualified bidder; the site breakdown is Athens High School $210,400.00, Boulan Park Middle School $105,200.00 and Larson Middle School $105,200.00. Mr. Robert Roop of Peter Basso Associates also reviewed the bids.

**Item 10.A – Bond Projects Update.** Barton Malow and TMP present "Troy School District 2013 Bond Program – Series 1, Construction Update 03.03.15." Troy High School classroom and storage additions and Boulan Park and Larson Middle School office additions carry completion dates of approximately December 2015; the Troy Athens LGI and multi-use classroom renovation is set for spring 2015. Planned 2015 bid packages: BP #8 Athens mechanical and electrical upgrades; BP #9 Larson and Boulan Park upgrades, window replacement and paving; BP #11 International Academy East pool converted to an LGI room; BP #12 Schroeder and Troy Union Elementary bus loop and canopies; BP #13 Smith Middle School and Niles Community High School gymnasium and restroom renovations.

**Items 10.B and 10.C – policy first readings.** B-0102, Board Members' Term of Office, sets a term of six (6) years commencing with the general school election in November of 2016 and on the November general election date in even years thereafter (adopted January 15, 2008). B-1202, Place of Meeting, locates meetings at the District Administrative Centers unless otherwise announced at least twenty-four hours in advance with notice posted per law (adopted April 8, 1975; revised March 15, 1977, January 16, 1979, April 15, 2003). B-1204, Quorum, provides that four members of the Board constitute a quorum, permits remote participation with the presiding chair's permission but without voting, and yields to the Open Meetings Act, MCL 15.261 et seq. (adopted January 16, 1979; revised July 10, 2012). B-1211, Public Participation in Board of Education Meetings, replaces 30 minutes of agenda-item comment at the beginning and 30 minutes of non-agenda comment at the end with public participation limited to 60 minutes per Board meeting, opening comment generally reserved for items posted as "Consideration." Speaker Request Forms are available 30 minutes prior to the start; recognized speakers get up to three (3) minutes (revised April 1988, March 17, 1998, July 10, 2007, March 17, 2009, April 20, 2010).
